recognize_zh: 骨髓切片免疫染色中，陽性（棕色）細胞呈線狀、條索狀聚集於竇狀隙內（intrasinusoidal），與周圍陰性的造血細胞分開，這種竇內分布型態是肝脾 T 細胞淋巴瘤的典型線索。
features: Bone marrow core with preserved fat and hypercellular hematopoietic tissue
Immunostain highlights cohesive clusters of positive cells arranged in linear and branching cords, conforming to sinusoidal spaces
Positive cells are small to medium-sized and densely packed within dilated sinusoids
Intervening interstitial hematopoietic cells are largely negative
Subtle intrasinusoidal distribution would be difficult to appreciate on H&E alone
describe_en: Bone marrow core biopsy immunostain shows a hypercellular marrow in which positive lymphoid cells are distributed predominantly within sinusoids, forming linear, branching and cord-like aggregates between fat spaces. The intervening hematopoietic elements are negative. The specific antibody is not labeled; the pattern is typical of a T-cell marker such as CD3. An intrasinusoidal T-cell infiltrate of this type is characteristic of hepatosplenic T-cell lymphoma in the appropriate clinical and immunophenotypic context (CD3+, CD4-/CD8-, TCR gamma-delta, cytotoxic TIA-1+/granzyme B-, isochromosome 7q).

ddx.vs: Also shows intrasinusoidal CD8+ T-cell rows but the cells are CD8+ and TCR alpha-beta with activated cytotoxic markers, lacking i(7q).
Cells are surface CD3-negative, CD56+, and EBER-positive, with a more interstitial and less sinusoid-restricted pattern.
Intrasinusoidal cells are large and CD20+/PAX5+ rather than small to medium T cells.
Reactive T cells are scattered and sparse rather than forming dense cohesive cords, and lack clonal TCR rearrangement.
